title: Token bucket limiter
description: Each client holds a bucket of tokens refilled at a fixed rate up to a burst capacity. Requests consume a token; empty buckets mean wait or reject. Token buckets allow bursts while enforcing the long-term rate, which matches how real clients behave. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers fixed-rate refill with burst capacity.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: {"rate": 5, "burst": 10, "want": 12}, 2: {"rate": 2, "burst": 4, "want": 6}, 3: {"rate": 10, "burst": 10, "want": 25}}
c = CFG[LEVEL]
tokens, allowed, denied = float(c["burst"]), 0, 0
for _ in range(c["want"]):
    tokens = min(c["burst"], tokens + c["rate"] * 0.1)
    if tokens >= 1: tokens -= 1; allowed += 1
    else: denied += 1
print("wanted %d: allowed %d, denied %d" % (c["want"], allowed, denied))
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Sliding window counter
description: Requests are counted in a sliding time window for precise enforcement: exactly N requests per rolling 60 seconds, not per calendar minute. Sliding windows close the boundary-exploit of fixed windows (2N requests straddling the boundary). Counters are kept per key. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers rolling-window precise counting.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: (10, 12), 2: (10, 8), 3: (5, 6)}
limit, want = CFG[LEVEL]
window = [0.0] * want  # request timestamps (simulated)
now = 100.0
count = sum(1 for t in window if now - t < 60)
allowed = min(want, max(0, limit - count))
print("limit %d/60s, wanted %d -> allowed %d, denied %d" % (limit, want, allowed, want - allowed))
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Per-key quotas
description: Limits are tracked separately per API key, user, or endpoint so one heavy consumer cannot starve others. Quota tables map keys to their limits and current usage. Per-key quotas are the foundation of fair multi-tenant service. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers separate limits per key/user/endpoint.

title: Quota exhaustion handling
description: When quota is exhausted the service returns 429 with a Retry-After header telling the client when to try again. Exhaustion responses are cheap to generate and never do partial work. Clients are expected to back off; repeat violators face tighter limits. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers 429 with Retry-After.
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Fair-share scheduling
description: When demand exceeds capacity, service is divided among tenants by weighted fair share rather than first-come-first-served. Weights reflect tiers or contracts. Fair-share prevents one tenant's flood from zeroing out everyone else during contention. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers weighted division under contention.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: {"a": 1, "b": 1}, 2: {"a": 3, "b": 1}, 3: {"a": 5, "b": 1, "c": 1}}
CAP = 100
w = CFG[LEVEL]
total = sum(w.values())
for t, wt in w.items():
    print("tenant", t, "weight", wt, "-> share:", round(CAP * wt / total))
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.
